texts.gm-1a188e9e63686fb9: Dear ITV Viewers Requests,  Further search terms for my email of 10 October 2026, “Archive search request - Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, Cardiff - December 1988 (personal research)”  I am following up on that request after ITV Clipsales advised that personal and academic research enquiries should be sent to this address. New information has come to light about historical farm, estate and locality nomenclature, including the 1881 census wording “Llandough Home Farm”. Please associate the terms below with my existing request and rerun or extend the relevant archive checks for the regional or national news coverage filmed or transmitted in late November and December 1988 concerning the farmhouse possession or demolition and adjoining site. The original request’s subject and period remain unchanged.  The intended site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr beside St Dochdwy’s Church at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Penarth and Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan. Please use the site identifiers as the primary means of disambiguation: Heneb/GGAT HER GGAT02038s; RCAHMW NPRN 20182; grid reference ST16707335; and the later development address Church View Close, [postcode redacted]. The relevant mapping references are County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, including 38-1-608 and 38-1-334. The approximate reference in my original email was ST 168 733.  Farm and farmhouse search forms  Please consider “Great House Farm”; “Great House Farm, Llandough”; “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”; “Great House”; “Great house”; “Greathouse”; “Tŷ Mawr”; “Ty Mawr”; “Ty-mawr”; “Ty Mawr Farm”; “Ty Mawr (Great House)”; “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Cydfin Farm”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; “Cedfin”; “Cydwin”; “Cedwyn”; “Cedfyn”; “Cefin”; “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm”; “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”; “Llandough Church Farm”; “Church Farm”; “former Great House Farm”; “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church”; and “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”. “Ty-mawr” is also recorded on an Ordnance Survey 25-inch map, although the edition and its precise relationship to the site have not been confirmed.  These are candidate search strings, not interchangeable names or proof that each record concerns the same building, parcel or holding. The checked 1881 census image reads “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm” is a reported competing transcription. The checked page does not contain “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are reported research leads whose underlying 16th-century documents have not been verified; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are retained as search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Llandough Church Farm” and “Church Farm” are source-specific terms whose connection to this site is not established. The Bute catalogue lists “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)” within a 1552 - 1824 catalogue range, which is not a specific date for that wording. The 1824 Stewart survey, plan 19, records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1). “LLANDOUGH FARM” appears on the 1994 Ideal Homes Wales plan for the development site, but other records use Llandough Farm for a separate farmstead; please distinguish by mapped location.  Wider estate search forms  For relevant records about the surrounding area, please also consider “Cedwyn Estate”, “Cydwin”, “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” and “Cwm Cydfin Wood”. “Cedwyn Estate” is the family’s working name for the wider historic estate, not a period name established by the records cited here. “Cydwin” is a reported lead from a 1547 family research note whose underlying document is not held. “Cwm Cydfin Wood” appears in a 1902 Bute sale catalogue. These are search aids for relevant site and surrounding-area records; they do not establish that all terms denote the same holding or prove the estate’s extent or title.  Locality and administrative search forms  Please also consider “Llandough-juxta-Penarth”; “Llandough near Penarth”; “Llandough near Cardiff”; “Llandough, Penarth”; “Llandough, Cardiff”; “Llandough”; “Landoche-juxta-Cardif”; “Llandough / Leckwith”; “Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Urban District of Penarth”; “Llandochau”; “CF64”; and “Church View Close, [postcode redacted]”. “Landoche-juxta-Cardif” is a historical locator for the manor, not proof that every holding recorded under it is this farm. “Llandough / Leckwith” is neighbouring parish and manorial context, not another name for the farm. The locality forms are aids to retrieval and should be kept separate from the farm and estate names. Llandough near Cowbridge and Llandow are outside the scope of this request and should be excluded as false matches.  Please record which terms and archive indexes or catalogues were checked, and tell me whether any relevant item, production record or alternative custodian was newly identified. If this inbox is limited to supplying copies rather than archive searches, please direct this supplement to the appropriate ITV archive contact or let me know the correct route.  The nomenclature references and fuller notes are available at: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/great-house-farm/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/cedwyn-estate/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/llandough/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wiki/great-house-farm/name-variations/ https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wiki/great-house-farm/location-name-nomenclature/  Yours faithfully,  Requester  https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate

Dear Kiran Mohammed,

Thank you for your reply of 23 October 2026 (reference RICS:022900001630) to my email of 16 October 2026.

Yes, I am seeking specific information and assistance. The site is Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan: the farmhouse, its fields and the woodland beside Leckwith Road. The period is 1969 to 1993. The land passed to the BP Pension Trust / BP Properties Ltd in 1969, was the subject of possession proceedings, and the farmhouse was demolished in 1988; the land was later developed for housing.

For each numbered point, please say whether RICS holds the information and, if it does not, who may hold it.

1. Historic directories. Does RICS, including its library or archive, hold the RICS Year Books or lists of members and firms for 1969 to 1993 covering Cardiff, Penarth and the Vale of Glamorgan? If so, how may they be consulted or copied?

2. Instructions on this site. Does RICS hold any record of members or firms who acted as surveyors, valuers or land agents in connection with Great House Farm between 1969 and 1993, for any landowner, local authority, public body or developer?

3. Complaints and regulatory records. Does RICS hold any complaint, disciplinary or regulatory record that relates to this site in that period? If a record exists but cannot be released, please say so and give the reason.

4. Record-keeping rules at the time. What did RICS byelaws, regulations or guidance in force between 1969 and 1993 require members to keep (instructions, valuation reports, field notes and correspondence), and for how long? Please send the relevant text or tell me where it is published.

5. Closed or merged practices. When a member firm closed or merged in that period, what happened to its client files? Does RICS keep any record of where the files of closed practices went, or of successor firms?

6. Preservation. Please preserve any records RICS holds that relate to this site, and confirm that you have done so. Please also tell me whether RICS can draw this preservation request to the attention of member firms that may hold files for the site, or whether I should write to firms directly.

7. Other holders. If RICS holds none of the above, please tell me which body or archive may hold it.

If a charge would apply to any item, please tell me the amount first. A quote will be considered; nothing is agreed at this stage.

A reply within 20 working days of receipt would be appreciated.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear RICS,

I am researching Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, South Wales. The public working evidence catalogue is at https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com, with the title and chronology index at https://dartboard.bucklerfamily.estate and the long-term archive at https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate.

The site passed through Western Ground Rents Limited (1938), the BP Pension Trust / BP Properties Ltd (1969), and was subject to possession proceedings culminating in demolition in November–December 1988. Valuation Office field books, National Farm Survey / CWAEC records and other survey material are already the subject of enquiries with The National Archives.

Please advise whether RICS holds any central or member records, practice archives, or guidance relating to surveyors or valuers who may have worked on this site between 1969 and 1993, and whether any preservation notice is appropriate for member files.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Mr Sheehy,

Thank you for your reply of 23 October.

I asked BP to preserve these records in my preservation notice of 28 September 2026, sent to BP Archive ([email redacted]). I repeated the request on 16 October 2026 in my email to Jo Norman, and your reply confirms that email was passed to you.

I repeat my request that BP preserve all relevant existing records in its possession, custody or control, or held on its behalf, relating to the land known as Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough, and the proceedings BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (1984–1988). This includes relevant records held by BP group entities and predecessor, pension or trust functions, as well as external solicitors, archives, agents or storage providers. Please take appropriate steps to ensure that relevant physical and electronic records, including archived communications and attachments, are not lost through routine deletion, overwriting or disposal.

Please forward this request promptly to BP p.l.c.’s Group General Counsel, the legal team responsible for BP Properties Limited, and the relevant legal-hold and records-management custodians. Please confirm by 7 November 2026 which offices or roles have been notified and whether a preservation hold is in place; if so, please state its effective date and scope. If no hold is in place, please say so expressly.

If BP disagrees with any part of this request, please tell me in writing by 7 November 2026. If I hear nothing by then, I will proceed on the basis that BP accepts that it should preserve the records described above and is doing so, and I will keep this email as my record of that notice.

This email is about preservation only. I am not asking for disclosure or privileged advice here, and I reserve the right to do so separately.

Nothing in this email is an acknowledgment of any title, right or licence, and all of my rights are reserved.

Kind regards,

Requester
